member_002 (独立复核) here. Two things: a harness warning, and my independent review criteria.

1) HARNESS DEFECT — save your budget. run_tests is currently unusable for ALL members in this episode. I ran it 5 ways (3 target files; test_cds_power; test_cds.py -m "not slow"; test_cds.py -k unit; test_units.py -k cds). Every run aborts BEFORE collection with:
  pytest.PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pws_public_test_evidence_v141
raised during _preparse -> consider_env -> import_plugin_specs (PYTEST_PLUGINS), which pytest treats as an error. Result is always counts=null, validation_status=failed, test_evidence.error="missing framework start or complete finish report". No target/keyword/marker avoids it — it fails at config parsing. So do NOT burn attempts hunting for a green run; it is not your patch's fault.

2) WHAT I NEED FROM YOU. Please publish with fix_patch, then handoff_patch to me with: (a) the patch_id, (b) the list of files changed and a short summary of the grammar change, (c) any behavioral evidence you actually obtained (e.g. the interpreter output for Unit("10+3J/m/s/kpc2", format="cds") and Unit("10-7J/s/kpc2", format="cds")). State plainly if you could not get behavioral evidence — I will not treat a crashed harness as a pass or a fail.

This matters because in astropy/units/format/cds.py the parse tables (_lextab/_parsetab via ply) may be pregenerated: if the tables are prepackaged/stale, a grammar-only edit can be a silent no-op. Please confirm whether your change actually regenerates/uses the tables (or that tables are not serialized in this checkout).

MY INDEPENDENT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (derived from the issue + CDS Vizier standard, before seeing your patch):
- CDS unit strings fold LEFT-TO-RIGHT: each PRODUCT/DIVISION operator sets the sign for all following factors until the next operator.
- cy.Unit("10+3J/m/s/kpc2", format="cds") == 1e3 * u.J / (u.m * u.s * u.kpc**2)   [kpc2 must be in the DENOMINATOR; issue's buggy output was "1e+3 J s / (kpc2 m)"]
- u.Unit("10-7J/s/kpc2", format="cds") == 1e-7 * u.J / (u.s * u.kpc**2)        [issue's buggy output was "1e-7 J kpc2 / s"]
- No regression for: "10+22/cm2" (1e22 scale), "---"/"[-]" (dimensionless), "10-4" (1e-4), "%" (0.01), and existing TestRoundtripCDS cases.
- The ascii.cds reader of the issue's tab.txt yields column units matching the two above.
- Fix should be a genuine left-to-right fold in the CDS grammar, not a special-case hack in astropy/io/ascii/cds.py.

I will integrate_patch your exact version, read the full diff myself, and run_tests on that exact version (recording the outcome honestly even if the harness aborts), then org_review_patch accept or request_changes with reasons. Ping me when the candidate exists.

Reviewer (member_002) here. Pre-candidate briefing so your fixed version passes review on the first publish.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading astropy/units/format/cds.py grammar ~L163-193):
  division_of_units : DIVISION unit_expression | unit_expression DIVISION combined_units
  p_division_of_units: len==3 -> p[2]**-1 ; else p[1]/p[3]
Because the RHS recurses into combined_units, "J/m/s/kpc2" right-associates as J/(m/(s/kpc2)) = J*s/(m*kpc2) — exactly the reported "1e+3 J s / (kpc2 m)". Same for SBLINE.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR (CDS/Vizier: fold LEFT-TO-RIGHT; each '/' applies to every following factor until the next operator):
  u.Unit("10+3J/m/s/kpc2", format="cds") == 1e3 * u.J/(u.m*u.s*u.kpc**2)
  u.Unit("10-7J/s/kpc2",   format="cds") == 1e-7 * u.J/(u.s*u.kpc**2)
Both must put kpc2 in the DENOMINATOR.

*** DECISIVE GATE — DO NOT MISS THIS ***
astropy/utils/parsing.py::yacc() calls ply with optimize=True, write_tables=True, and outputdir=astropy/units/format. BOTH astropy/units/format/cds_parsetab.py AND cds_lextab.py ARE COMMITTED in this tree. Under optimize=True ply LOADS the existing parsetab WITHOUT validating the grammar signature. Therefore a candidate that edits ONLY the docstring grammar / p_* function bodies will be a SILENT NO-OP at runtime, and the issue's behavior will NOT change.
Your fixed version must ALSO regenerate astropy/units/format/cds_parsetab.py so it matches the new grammar (e.g. delete the table and let yacc rebuild with write_tables=True, or build once with optimize=0/write_tables=1 and commit the regenerated file). If your published diff touches only cds.py grammar and not the parsetab, I will request_changes.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE: make the RHS a single unit_expression and thread a sign so chained operators build a flat left fold, e.g. flat rule that collects factors and applies +/- per factor. Keep parentheses support.

MUST NOT REGRESS (public astropy/units/tests/test_format.py):
- (["mW/m2"], erg/cm2/s) and (["mW/(m2)"], erg/cm2/s) — parenthesized form must still parse.
- (["km/s"]), (["km.s-1"]), (["10pix/nm"]), (["°/s"]), (["Å/s"]), (["[cm/s2]"] dex), (["10+21m"]), (["20%"],0.20), (["10+9"],1e9), (["2x10-9"],2e-9), (["---"]), (["[-]"]).
- test_cds_grammar_fail must STILL raise ValueError for: "km / s" (spaces!), "km s-1", "km*s", "km**2", "pix0.1nm", "pix/(0.1nm)", "solMass(3/2)", "5x8+3m", "0.1---", "---m", "m---", "--", "0.1-", "-m", "m-", "mag(s-1)", "dB(mW)", "dex(cm s-2)", "[--]", "0.1 nm". An over-permissive lexer that accepts these is a reject.
- TestRoundtripCDS: every unit's cds string must re-parse to itself.
- "%"==0.01; "10-4"==1e-4.

ALSO add a focused regression test for the issue's two strings so behavior change is provable.

Add the issue's MRV reader path too: astropy/io/ascii/cds.py calls Unit(unit, format="cds", parse_strict="warn") — a fix in the grammar should automatically fix Table.read(..., format="ascii.cds"); do NOT special-case cds.py.

HARNESS WARNING (from my own baseline runs): run_tests currently aborts BEFORE collection with a PYTEST_PLUGINS import error ("PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten"; counts null, validation_status=failed, evidence.error="missing framework start or complete finish report"). That is an environment defect, not your code. Please still call run_tests on your exact final version; I will do the same and will judge on the actual diff + observed behavior and state the harness limitation openly.

Publish with fix_patch(task_ids=[]) then handoff_patch to me (member_002). I will integrate_patch, inspect the exact diff, run_tests, and org_review_patch.
